sermon.title: No One Knows the Day, Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that no one knows the day or hour of Christ’s return, then walks through the pre-tribulation rapture teaching and a long history of failed end-time predictions, from 400 AD to Y2K and 2012. He warns that such predictions distract believers from the great commandment, make the church look foolish and confuse new Christians, and says God’s signs will be supernatural.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he gives “1 Chronicles 12:38” for the children of Issachar; that verse is 1 Chronicles 12:32 (shown). He cites “Acts 1:6” for “it is not for you to know the times or seasons,” which is Acts 1:7 (shown). His history of predictions names many real people, churches and groups (popes, reformers, explorers, preachers, authors, healers and religious movements); those names, dates and his statements about them, including that some authors profited from wrong predictions, are his own and are not verified here. Some names are given as the captions heard them, and a few words are marked [unclear].

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, darkness which may even be felt.” So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days. They did not see one another; nor did anyone rise from his place for three days. But all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

But as one was cutting down a tree, the iron ax head fell into the water; and he cried out and said, “Alas, master! For it was borrowed.” So the man of God said, “Where did it fall?” And he showed him the place. So he cut off a stick, and threw it in there; and he made the iron float. Therefore he said, “Pick it up for yourself.” So he reached out his hand and took it.
Now it was about the sixth hour, and there was darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour. Then the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in two.

faqs.question: Have people always tried to predict Christ’s return?
faqs.answer: He says mankind has been trying to predict it ever since Christ left the earth, beginning in the early church.

faqs.question: Is Christ king now, or only after He returns?
faqs.answer: He says Christ is ruling now, His kingdom is eternal, “and he’s always been a king and he always will be a king.”

faqs.question: Is the mid-tribulation view still taught?
faqs.answer: He says he doesn’t meet anybody with mid-trib anymore; it is pre-trib or post-trib.

faqs.question: Why does he warn against idolizing end-time teachers?
faqs.answer: He says everybody claims, “I got revelation this is how it’s going to work out I got a chart,” and we idolize them and buy their books instead of reading the Bible for ourselves.

faqs.question: Why does he talk about an infatuation with 666?
faqs.answer: He says predictions were tied to 666 years after the rise of Islam and to the year 1666, showing an infatuation with the antichrist and numerology that has gone on for centuries.

faqs.question: What happened in the 1833 meteor shower?
faqs.answer: He says meteors lit up the night for about four hours so that you could read a newspaper, and everybody thought “this is it,” some even waiting on the roof for the rapture.

faqs.question: What happened after the 1844 prediction failed?
faqs.answer: He says it was called the great disappointment; some people killed themselves and others were destitute because they had sold their properties and means of living.

faqs.question: What does he say about predicting the end after your death?
faqs.answer: He jokes, “if you’re going to predict something predict it after your death nobody can attack you.”

faqs.question: Could Christ come any minute before 1967?
faqs.answer: He says prophets taught He could come any minute, then said 1967 fulfilled the times of the Gentiles so He can come, which means “he couldn’t have come any minute before.”

faqs.question: Did Jesus heal people who had no belief?
faqs.answer: He asks, “Did Jesus ever do that did he ever heal people that had no belief. Yes he did.”

faqs.question: Why did he know Y2K would not destroy the world?
faqs.answer: He says he was trained in computers, which “only can put out what you put into it,” and he researched and talked to knowledgeable people in the field.

faqs.question: Was the darkness at the cross an eclipse?
faqs.answer: He says no eclipse lasts for three hours; “It was a supernatural darkening of the day.”
